claims.text: Multi-element grain-boundary segregation will improve the mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
The mechanical improvement will result from inhibition of grain-boundary sliding and migration.
Grain-boundary decoration can improve mechanical performance without significantly changing the magnetocaloric effect.
Conventional, unmodified grain boundaries are responsible for the mechanical instability, fatigue, or cracking of the baseline MnNiSi-based material.
The baseline MnNiSi-based material exhibits a large magnetocaloric effect.
A tailored thermal or post-processing treatment can induce multi-element segregation at grain boundaries.
The proposed processing treatment can promote well-distributed twin boundaries in MnNiSi-based materials.
Selecting non-magnetic or weakly magnetic segregants will ensure that the bulk magnetic entropy change remains large.
Controlled annealing can facilitate multi-element segregation without significant grain growth.
Processing below a magnetic-ordering threshold will avoid altering the magnetic ordering of the MnNiSi matrix.
Multi-element grain-boundary segregation reduces grain-boundary energy.
Multi-element segregation reduces the thermodynamic driving force for grain growth and can stabilize grain boundaries.
Twin boundaries provide barriers to dislocation motion.
Introducing twin boundaries enhances ductility in the proposed MnNiSi-based material.
Segregants that do not disrupt the magnetic lattice will preserve the large magnetocaloric effect.
The treated material will have increased yield strength and improved fatigue resistance relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated material's peak magnetic entropy change and relative cooling power will remain close to the untreated baseline.
The proposed strengthening strategy applies primarily to nanocrystalline or fine-grained MnNiSi materials in which grain-boundary-mediated deformation predominates.
An improvement of less than approximately 10% in yield strength or fatigue life counts as failure to achieve the proposed mechanical benefit.
Retention of ΔSm and RCP within 10% of control values constitutes acceptable preservation of magnetocaloric performance.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis presents twin-boundary formation as optional ('possibly in combination'), whereas the intervention and structural mediator treat twin-boundary promotion and enhanced twin density as integral parts of the intervention.
